passage: Sit, Shalini. This old man, Akash, once lost a ball beneath the old sofa. I was nine. My arm went in up to the shoulder and my fingers touched nothing but dust. My sister was giggling at me. Then I stopped asking myself, how do I reach it, and I asked, does my hand have to be the one that gets it? The ball only had to come out. So I ran to my school bag, pulled out my long steel ruler, lay flat on the floor, and pushed the ball gently sideways until it rolled into the light. It is funny, beta. The sofa never changed. Only my question did.

qa.q: What did Akash use to get the ball out?
qa.a: Akash used the long steel ruler from the school bag to push the ball gently sideways until it rolled into the light.

qa.q: What was Akash feeling with an arm under the sofa, touching only dust?
qa.a: Akash was frustrated, and probably a little embarrassed with the sister giggling nearby.

qa.q: What was the turning point in the story, and why did it help?
qa.a: Akash changed the question from how to reach the ball to what would get it out, which opened up the idea of pushing it with a ruler.

qa.q: How might the sister have seen it when the ball rolled out?
qa.a: The sister, who had been giggling, may have been surprised and impressed that a ruler solved it after the reaching failed.

grounding: Shows Akash changing a stuck reach into a push and using a ruler from the school bag.

passage:
The school van would honk in five minutes, and Mridul's cricket ball had rolled under the heavy sofa. His hand went in up to the elbow. Nothing. The gap was too low and too deep.
His sister Arohi said, "Leave it. Get it in the evening."
"I need it for the match at lunch," Mridul said. He lay flat and looked under. The ball was at the back, near the wall.
He sat up and thought. "I can't reach it. But I don't need to reach it. I just need to push it out the other side."
He grabbed the long wooden ruler from his school bag, slid it along the floor behind the ball from the side, and pushed. The ball rolled out by Arohi's feet.
The van honked. Mridul stuffed the ball and ruler into his bag and ran.

qa.q: What did Mridul use to push the ball?
qa.a: He used the long wooden ruler from his school bag.

qa.q: How was Mridul feeling when his hand could not reach the ball?
qa.a: He was worried and a bit desperate, since the van was coming and he needed the ball for the lunch match.

qa.q: What else could Mridul have tried if the ruler was too short?
qa.a: He could have asked Arohi to help lift one end of the sofa a little, or used a broom handle.

qa.q: How might Arohi see Mridul's trick?
qa.a: Arohi may be surprised and impressed, since she had told him to leave it and he got it out in seconds.

grounding: It shows a boy who cannot reach a ball under a sofa changing the problem from reaching to pushing, and using a long ruler from his bag.

Jomon's tennis ball had bounced under the low wooden divan in his grandmother's flat in Kochi. He lay on the floor and stretched his arm in. His fingers touched the tip of the fuzzy ball and pushed it further back. Worse.
His friend Darshan knelt beside him. "Now it's stuck forever."
Jomon sat back on his heels. He didn't try again at once. "Wait. Why am I trying to grab it? If I push it from behind, it has to come out the front."
"But you can't reach behind it."
"My hand can't." Jomon unzipped his school bag and pulled out his thirty-centimetre ruler. He slid it along the floor, around the side of the ball, and flicked it toward himself.
The ball rolled out across the floor. Darshan caught it and laughed. "Genius!"

qa.q: Whose flat was the divan in?
qa.a: It was in his grandmother's flat in Kochi.

qa.q: What was Jomon thinking when he sat back on his heels?
qa.a: He was calm and curious, realising he didn't need to grab the ball but could push it out from behind.

qa.q: What would change if Jomon had kept stretching his arm?
qa.a: He might have pushed the ball further back and got frustrated, instead of finding a new way to solve it.

qa.q: How does Darshan see Jomon's idea?
qa.a: Darshan thinks it's stuck forever at first, then is delighted and calls Jomon a genius when the ball rolls out.

grounding: It shows a boy reframing a stuck ball from reaching to pushing it out, and using a long ruler from his bag.
